replacement: glf expression (plus a glucokinase, e.g. glk, for phosphorylation)
biological_effect: reduce PEP consumption during glucose uptake
mechanism: the PTS glucose transport system (encoded partly by ptsG) consumes one PEP per glucose molecule imported; replacing PTS-mediated uptake with a non-PTS glucose facilitator (glf) paired with a glucokinase spares PEP for other PEP-dependent biosynthetic reactions
expected_effect: increased PEP availability for PEP-dependent biosynthetic reactions (e.g. DAHP synthase, the first committed step of the shikimate pathway)
risk: non-PTS glucose uptake can reduce glucose uptake rate and growth rate compared to native PTS transport
evidence: general, well-established central-carbon-metabolism engineering pattern (PTS replacement for PEP conservation); not a specific verified experimental result from any single paper in this V1.1 knowledge base - see knowledge/papers/ for what is actually cited

biological_effect: reduce competitive PEP consumption via glycolysis
mechanism: pyruvate kinase (PykF, the major isozyme) converts PEP to pyruvate as part of central glycolytic flux; reducing its activity decreases competing consumption of PEP, preserving more of the pool for PEP-dependent biosynthetic reactions
expected_effect: increased intracellular PEP pool available for biosynthesis
risk: pykF knockout can impair growth by limiting pyruvate and acetyl-CoA supply to central energy metabolism, particularly under some carbon sources
evidence: general, well-established central-carbon-metabolism engineering pattern (pyruvate kinase attenuation for PEP conservation); not a specific verified experimental result from any single paper in this V1.1 knowledge base - see knowledge/papers/ for what is actually cited

biological_effect: provides an alternative, lower-carbon-loss route that can supply E4P and/or acetyl-phosphate, improving precursor availability for the aromatic amino acid pathway
mechanism: phosphoketolase converts fructose-6-phosphate to erythrose-4-phosphate and acetyl-phosphate (or xylulose-5-phosphate to glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate and acetyl-phosphate), bypassing carbon-losing decarboxylation steps of native central metabolism and directly supplementing the E4P pool used by DAHP synthase
expected_effect: improved E4P/precursor supply for the shikimate pathway
risk: heterologous enzyme expression adds metabolic burden; rebalancing flux through this route can have unintended effects on acetyl-CoA and acetate metabolism
evidence: general, well-established metabolic engineering pattern (phosphoketolase pathway introduction for E4P/acetyl-CoA supply); not a specific verified experimental result from any single paper in this V1.1 knowledge base - see knowledge/papers/ for what is actually cited

biological_effect: shift NADH/NADPH cofactor balance to support a heterologous pathway's redox cofactor requirements
mechanism: PntAB interconverts NADH and NADPH across the membrane; tuning its expression can rebalance cofactor pools when a heterologous pathway's redox cofactor demand does not match the host's native balance
expected_effect: improved cofactor availability for a heterologous biosynthetic pathway
risk: cofactor rebalancing can perturb unrelated NAD(P)H-dependent pathways and cellular redox state
evidence: general, well-established cofactor-engineering pattern for heterologous pathway support; not a specific verified experimental result from any single paper in this V1.1 knowledge base - see knowledge/papers/ for what is actually cited

biological_effect: rebalances central-metabolism precursor ratios by routing flux through the Entner-Doudoroff pathway alongside native glycolysis
mechanism: the Entner-Doudoroff pathway (6-phosphogluconate dehydratase/edd, KDPG aldolase/eda) produces pyruvate and glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate with a different stoichiometry than EMP glycolysis; combining it with the native route changes the ratio of precursors feeding the MEP pathway
risk: rewiring flux through an alternative route can affect growth and other pathways sharing the same precursor pools
evidence: general, well-established central-metabolism engineering pattern (Entner-Doudoroff pathway activation for precursor rebalancing), consistent with DDR-003's stated engineering pattern; not a specific verified experimental result from any single paper in this V1.1 knowledge base - see knowledge/papers/ for what is actually cited
